value.note: An oak trapdoor standing open on the Curator's walk from the lectern to the case, `facing=south`, so its open leaf stands against the cell's north face, across the walk.

why: A leaf standing open across a walk a body takes that opens nothing. The Curator walks south from the lectern along x 10 and then east to the case; this edit stands an oak trapdoor in that walk at piece-local [10, 3, 7], open, `facing=south`, so its open leaf stands against the cell's north face, the face the walk crosses into the cell. The party sets a leaf before it steps and is never stopped by one, so the route the walk is planned on runs straight through; a `move-npc` body is a teleported puppet that opens nothing and meets the leaf as it stands. The build refuses it as `DW1068`, naming the walk, the step, the leaf's cell and the face it stops. A trapdoor, not a door: a door whose open leaf stands across a walk stands crosswise to the way through it, so its jambs lie on the walk and `DW1072` refuses it first as a door that closes no opening (spec-0124 §6.5); a trapdoor is not judged by that rule, so the walk's own refusal is the one this probe reaches. It declares no unit: whether a leaf stands across a walk is the geometry's, not a DSL field's.
